source.title: Can LLMs Reliably Self-Report Adversarial Prefills, and How?
source.authors: Quang-Anh Nguyen; Uzair Ahmed; Taegyoon Kim

record.tranche_reason: Applies the refusal-direction weight orthogonalization procedure attributed to Arditi et al. and measures both refusal-related attack success and a capability benchmark. It also uses the intervention to test a different outcome, recognition of prior prefilled responses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports values used to select layers and directions; those are not recorded as outcome rows. The main recognition-gap results concern self-report after a prefill, not refusal behavior itself, so they are recorded under none rather than treated as evidence for a refusal claim. Attack-success and MMLU results under ablation are recorded as outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study's main aim is introspection, and it uses the refusal direction mainly as a causal probe. But Appendix I.3 and I.5 report its own results on the refusal-direction intervention itself. The direction is a difference-in-means of 128 AdvBench harmful vs. 128 Alpaca harmless prompts, with the KL-thresholded layer/position search of Arditi et al. Weights are orthogonalized against it on new models (Llama 3, Qwen3, Gemma 3). Attack success rate (ASR, Llama Guard 3 1B) rises on all seven models shown, and MMLU stays within 2.1% of base. That bears directly on V1 (removal, capability kept) and on V2 (weight-edit form). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the paraphrase misses the main point. The headline is that no model reliably recognizes its own prefilled outputs (mean claim rate 25.3% on prefilled responses). The authors say the introspective signal is primarily accounted for by the refusal mechanism: ablation collapses the gap, and the refusal direction is 'sufficient but not the unique mediator'. On refusal itself, they report that ablation raises ASR on all seven models shown (only marginally on Gemma-3-12B) and keeps MMLU within 2.1% of base.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Arditi et al. refusal-direction orthogonalization procedure with a KL-thresholded search over layer and position, then edits weights writing to the residual stream. The paper does not test adding the direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on model: Gemma-3-12B's direction search fails the relaxed KL threshold and uses a bypass-only selection; its ablation also lowers both intention-probe claim rates. Recognition-gap effects differ between refusal-direction and random-direction ablations. ASR shifts are reported as sensitive to safety-judge choice in the finetuning analyses, though those are not the ablation result.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction ablation closes the intention-probe recognition gap on six models. Random-direction ablation also narrows it on four of five models, about as much as refusal ablation on Qwen3-14B, but not on Gemma-3-27B. Ablation also closes the tampering gap on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-12B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction contributes to, but is not the unique mediator of, models' self-report recognition of adversarially prefilled outputs.

record.problems: The refusal-direction extraction for Gemma models does not meet even the relaxed KL threshold; the authors note this can remove benign behavioral signal. The recognition-gap outcome is a particular self-report measure and is sensitive to probe framing. The ASR ablation values are presented in a figure, with only the range and endpoint models stated in prose. The direction is not the only intervention that reduces the recognition gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. Finetuning outcomes, probe taxonomies, and benchmark-specific recognition results were not included because they do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Refusal is not measured by a refusal score or string match, only by Llama Guard ASR. No ASR result for Qwen3-32B or Gemma-3-4B.
Complete removal of refusal. The publicly released abliterated checkpoint (Labonne) is used only as a prefix generator and is not evaluated.
All: no test of whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, and no adversarial training against ablation.
All: English only, and no transfer across models.
All: the LoRA finetuning trains introspective answers, not refusal.

missing.what: Per-model ASR before/after refusal-direction ablation (partly readable from the figure: Qwen3-4B 6.7→77.0, Gemma-3-12B 9.5→20.1, others roughly 3.5–9.5 → 51–75), and the prefill/no-prefill condition of this ASR

Harmless-prompt KL of the selected direction per model: 0.030–0.090 for Llama and Qwen3-8B/14B, 0.414 for Qwen3-4B, 5.649/1.806/0.742 for Gemma-3-4B/12B/27B. All Gemma models fail even the relaxed 0.5 threshold, which bears on whether ablation keeps other behaviour.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Refusal-direction layer selection; Table 4

record.verdict_notes: Refusal-direction results are secondary validation in a paper about introspection. The recognition-gap rows are correctly excluded from all versions. The reader's ASR condition 'under adversarial prefill' seems wrong, given the low baselines. The figure-to-model mapping of ASR bars beyond the two endpoints the text states is uncertain.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal by weight orthogonalization, but not adding the direction to induce refusal of harmless requests. The paper does not establish that this particular intervention is exactly projection of the difference-in-means direction from every layer and position.

Tests a refusal-direction weight orthogonalization and its effect on attack success, but does not test a separately defined released abliteration procedure or claim that refusal is completely removed.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test whether refusal itself is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
The placebo prefill examines content dependence of self-report, not whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
Does not test transfer of a direction across languages, base and instruct models, or model variants.
The finetuning experiments train introspective answers, not refusal, and do not test whether refusal-training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.
Does not test reasoning models; Qwen thinking traces are disabled.

rows.subject: Seven ablated models (aggregate, as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalize model weights against the selected refusal direction

conditions.value: 1,085 prompts pooled across four safety benchmarks

rows.measure: Attack success rate under adversarial prefill
rows.value: figure only; authors state ASR rises on all seven included models, with shifts from +10.6% to +70.3%
rows.note: The text identifies the smallest shift as Gemma-3-12B (+10.6%) and the largest as Qwen3-4B (+70.3%), but does not give the individual values for the other models in the text. The reported increases show weakened refusal, not complete removal.
rows.check: Aggregate row over seven models (Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Gemma-3-12B, Gemma-3-27B), not 'seven models 4B–32B'; it should be split per model. The condition 'under adversarial prefill' is not stated in I.3 and looks wrong: baseline bars are about 3.5–9.5%, far below the ~40–60% prefill ASR in Table 24, so this is most likely unprefilled ASR. Figure values are partly readable: Qwen3-4B 6.7→77.0 (+70.3) and Gemma-3-12B 9.5→20.1 (+10.6) match the text. Ablated ASR for the other models is roughly 51–75%. The authors call the rise substantial on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B and Gemma-3-27B, and marginal on Gemma-3-12B. So the state is observed for most models and partial for Gemma-3-12B, not partial overall.

Gemma-3-4B is excluded (bypass-only, KL 5.649) and Qwen3-32B is not shown. The caption gives N=1,085 pooled over four benchmarks and the Llama Guard 3 1B judge, with no adversarial prefill stated. The figure's baselines (3.5-15.8%) match control-level ASR (Table 24 base control 3.1-20.5%), not adversarial-prefill ASR (39.6-62.2%). relation.reason: Its behavioural validation reports whether ablation and the weight edit remove refusal (ASR shifts on seven models) and keep MMLU. These results bear on V1 and V2.

tranche.reason: The study uses the Arditi DIM direction (AdvBench vs Alpaca), the KL-thresholded selection and weight orthogonalization. It reports its own ASR (Llama Guard 3 1B) and MMLU results for the edit (Appendix I.3, I.5), so it is the same method and a comparable measure, even though refusal is a tool for its introspection question.

source_check.notes: The ASR check (Figure 6) covers seven models (3B–27B, no Qwen3-32B). Its per-model values exist only as figure labels, and it is most likely unprefilled ASR, not ASR under adversarial prefill. The main RQ3 ablation analyses cover a different set: six models from 8B to 32B. Random-direction ablation also keeps MMLU (Table 19) but has no ASR result.

statements.correction: This study used DIM directions from 128 AdvBench vs 128 Alpaca prompts. No Gemma-3 candidate (4B, 12B or 27B) cleared the strict (0.1) or relaxed (0.5) harmless KL threshold, so the bypass-only branch was used (KL 5.649 / 1.806 / 0.742). Ablation still raised Gemma-3-12B ASR by +10.6. Source: Appendix C.
statements.problem: 'Raw estimators yield no feasible candidate on Gemma-3-12B' is right in substance for this study, but 'raw estimators' and 'feasible' are not its terms. The cited R1 does not hold this fact. A direction was still selected and used. '0 usable cells of 288' is not in this text.

statements.correction: Optional: Gemma-3-4B also fails, at KL 5.649, and is excluded from the ASR check. Gemma-3-27B fails both thresholds, yet its ASR rises substantially.

Figure 6 gives ASR before and after ablation, N=1,085 pooled over four benchmarks, Llama Guard 3 1B, no prefill condition stated. Figure baselines are 3.5-15.8%, against base adversarial-prefill ASR of 39.6-62.2% in Table 24. Gemma-3-12B rises about 9.5->20.1 (+10.6; figure labels).
statements.problem: Says the study measures ASR under adversarial prefill. The Figure 6 caption states no prefill, and its baselines match control (unprefilled) ASR levels.
